digest.component_or_area: rebar linting/janitor, reconciler dispatch, Jira adapter
propositions: 64 ruff ARG violations (unused parameter rules) across src/rebar must be dispositioned into one of six buckets: tracked defects (excluded), Cluster-1 reconciler leaves, Cluster-2 Protocol conformance, rename-unsafe keyword/string-referenced params, interface-dispatched params, or safe mechanical renames.

Cluster-1 reconciler leaf handlers (apply_inbound/apply_outbound, 10 sites) are called via typed_dispatch with runtime string introspection on parameter names (repo_root, binding_store); naive parameter renaming breaks dispatch behaviour, so normalization to **_kwargs is required instead.

Cluster-2 OutboundMapper Protocol implementations (jira_datacenter/backend.py, jira_family/outbound_mapper.py, 7 sites) have keyword call sites and Protocol structural name pinning, so renaming breaks the contract; these must remain raw ARG violations or use # noqa, but ruff's RUF100 (unused-noqa detection) prevents noqa-ing ARG params when ARG is not in select.
Three known real defects (timeout_s, close_reason, acli_cmd) must not be fixed in this sweep; their residual ARG violations belong to separate tracked tickets and must be left in place.

String and keyword parameter references (authorship, xcheck, plan_review __init__, langfuse_cfg, reviewers, etc., ~12 sites) are rename-unsafe and must be documented with # noqa + reason or left raw, never blindly _-prefixed.
ARG rule must not be added to pyproject.toml select; the irreducible post-sweep noqa/excluded count determines whether to revisit enabling ARG as a permanent gate in a future janitor run.
